description: Executed grounding for the registry's figure receipts: the frozen renderer re-renders the historical registry states (74 and 75 evals) and its bytes are matched against the committed figures, byte for byte; the frozen second-code-path checker is re-run on the committed sidecars (both accepted with the exact PASS line), on a stale sidecar and two authored attacks (each caught, with the exact fail lines reproduced), and the degenerate registries are shown to die at their documented spots. The fresh-sidecar round trip — render, then let the checker accept the render's own sidecar — is executed by this package's gates, which spawn the pinned checker against the invocation's own output and then require those fresh sidecars to be byte-identical to the committed historical ones modulo exactly the one source field — the absolute path of the run's own copy of the registry, which the gate separately requires to resolve to bytes with the pinned registry hash.
notes: rcos-eval/2: this package declares NO adapter of its own. It names the registered
capability and the input document, and the run reaches the capability through the
invocation kernel — `rcos run receipt-figure-render --input ...` takes the identical
path. The thing being evaluated is the thing reuse will call.
This replaces NOTHING. The two eval entries already on the registry entry
('registry-verdict-figures' and the regeneration-after-change one) are historical
assertions and stay byte-for-byte as written; this receipt is a new record that links
backward by exercising the SAME frozen scripts (receipt_figures.py, sha256 d4acec84…,
and check_figures.py, sha256 a4a51bfe…, both pinned in gates/check.js) on the SAME
committed bytes the historical logs point at.
Every historical fact is reproduced, not invented. The four oracle figures and the two
historical sidecars are byte-identical to the files committed under
evidence/receipt-figure-render/: eval-1/{fig-verdicts.png f432049f…,
fig-per-capability.png 83e6f3d5…, values.json 12420d1b…} and
eval-2/{fig-verdicts.png 384e4fda…, fig-per-capability.png 1fb79b8c…,
values.json e871124f…}; the attack sidecar values-tampered.json (4d09e7b6…) is
evidence/receipt-figure-render/attack/values-tampered.json. The registry state behind
eval-1 is registry-74.json, which is byte-identical to
`git show 73cdbfd:registry/capability-registry.json` (20 capabilities, 74 evals; the
only zero-eval capability at that commit is receipt-figure-render itself). The
eval-2/logged regeneration state is registry-75-reconstructed.json: 20 capabilities,
75 evals, and exactly ONE entry differs from the 74 state — receipt-figure-render,
which gained the one eval those figures were regenerated for. No capability was added
or removed in that move, so the historical claim 're-rendered after the registry moved
74->75' is exercised against that single-entry delta.
Ten cases: five renders (the two historical states, one authored boundary state, and
the two degenerate registries) and five checks (two historical acceptances, a stale
sidecar, and two authored attacks). There is deliberately NO check case that names a
previous case's output: the adapter's work dir is the INVOCATION work dir while `{work}`
in capability_input resolves to the RUNNER work dir — different directories — so the
render->check round trip is executed by the gates instead. gates/fresh_sidecars_accepted
spawns the pinned check_figures.py against the invocation's freshly rendered sidecar
for both historical registries (the same pattern as re-extracting a frame with ffmpeg in
a gate), and gates/fresh_sidecar_reproduces_historical then compares those fresh sidecar
bytes with the committed historical fixture bytes. The acceptance therefore rests on bytes
the run itself produced, judged by the frozen checker through a fresh process.
The 21-capability state (registry-21-caps.json) has ZERO historical lineage and is
labeled as such: it is the 74-eval registry plus one authored capability,
audit-control-probe, with zero evals. It exists to measure a boundary fact rather than
to retell history: figure 1 is a function of the verdict distribution ALONE, so its
fig-verdicts.png is byte-identical to the 74 state's, while figure 2 grows by one
36-pixel row whose bars are both empty. The two degenerate registries
(empty-registry.json, malformed-registry.json) are authored too — neither ever appears
in any historical log, and the eval asserts what the frozen renderer actually does
with them, not what it ought to do.
The two attacks are authored controls with zero lineage. values-tampered.json is the
committed attack sidecar: verdict_distribution ship 65->99, so the checker must name
that one field and nothing else. values-cap-shifted.json moves two capabilities' ship
counts in opposite directions so every total still agrees (muse-image-lane 2->1 and
chalk-capture-recipe 2->3; n_capabilities, n_evals and verdict_distribution are all
unchanged), so only the per_capability comparison can catch it — measured, the checker
names exactly those two capabilities and nothing else. The stale case gives the 74
registry the 75 sidecar; measured, the checker reports THREE lines in a fixed order
(n_evals, then verdict_distribution, then per_capability). Each of those inputs is
accepted somewhere else in this package (both sidecars pass on their own registry,
values-tampered and values-cap-shifted are the 74 sidecar with one field moved), so each
catch is attributable to the combination under test, not to a broken input.
Documented limitations of the frozen pair, asserted rather than papered over:
* the renderer writes fig-verdicts.png BEFORE it builds figure 2, so an empty
registry crashes at receipt_figures.py's max() over an empty sequence with figure
1 already on disk and no sidecar and no figure 2; a malformed registry dies in
json.load with NO outputs at all. The asymmetry is measured, not assumed.
* check_figures.py never reads the sidecar's `source` field — all four fixture
sidecars carry the same real registry path in `source`, and the attacks still bite
on the four numeric fields, so `source` is recorded but never verified. This eval
says so in the notes instead of implying the field is checked.
* check_figures.py never opens the PNGs. Byte-level figure equality is therefore
established in this package's own gates, which decode the rendered PNGs
(bit_depth 8, color_type 2, filter types 0-4) and re-simulate the frozen pixel
model from the registry fixture directly — never from the sidecar it is checking.
The pixel model these gates simulate was measured against the oracle bytes, not
assumed: PIL rectangle fills are inclusive of both endpoints, later rectangles
overwrite shared boundary pixels, figure 1's scale is 600/max(1,n_evals) with rows at
y 70..110 and x starting at 30 with 24px gaps, and figure 2 is 900 wide by 100+36n
tall with bars from x=290 at 610/max_ev per eval.
The one nondeterminism in the frozen checker is recorded rather than hidden: for a
multi-key per_capability diff, the fail line's entries come out of a Python set, so
their ORDER varies with PYTHONHASHSEED. The capability-shift gate therefore asserts the
line's shape, the id set, and each (sidecar, recompute) pair as substrings, never the
exact byte order; the single-key diffs and the distribution dict are deterministic and
are asserted as exact lines.
Pins are metadata, not measurements: every sha256 and byte count in this package was
computed from the committed files on this box, and the gates re-derive the figure
geometry from the registry fixtures themselves, so a wrong source, a wrong seek, or a
wrong count FAILS the run instead of riding along in the record.
The frozen scripts are executed by their recorded home-relative paths
(capabilities/receipt-figure-render/adapter/{receipt_figures.py,check_figures.py}) and
are never written through: the eval runner copies the registry fixtures into the run
work dir and the adapter reads them in place through the paths each case declares,
writing only under its own invocation work dir; the frozen_source_pinned gate re-hashes
both scripts after the run.
